title: Out of the circle
goals: A trial with its name and its colour.
The book can conjure it in one line.
Your familiar has left the circle.
It is on the moon's plate.
starting_code:
class {familiar_class}(Familiar):
    def __init__(self, name, color):
        self.name = name
        self.color = color

{familiar_var} = {familiar_class}("{familiar}", "{familiar_color}")
wizard.cast("minka", {familiar_var})

# The plates on the floor are three objects: `moon`, `sun` and `star`. Each has its attribute `position`: `print(moon.position)` tells you which cell the moon is on.

# Two steps down with `move_down`, and it is out of the circle.

# Four steps to the left with `move_left`.

# Five steps up with `move_up`, to the moon's plate.
hints: Your familiar inherits from `Familiar` the same moves your `wizard` has.
A move is used with the dot, with your familiar's variable before it.
Three moves: two steps down, four to the left and five up.
intro:
Remember that while your familiar is in the circle, you can undo it and describe another. If you take it out, it will live.

Think it over well before you take it out, and then take it to the moon's plate.
outro: {familiar} lives. It breathes, it casts a shadow, and it is looking at you.
learned: Now you know that your familiar walks with moves you never wrote, inherited from `Familiar`, with the same names as your `wizard`'s, and that an object is used with the dot, whether its class is the game's or yours.

told.go:
If you are sure, go ahead.

I will write your description and your conjuring in the book of Arvelia, and it will be conjured for ever.
told.not_yet:
That is not how it works: if you are sure you want to make your familiar…

…you need to take it out and lead it to the right place.
told.halt:
Stop! You have already completed this level, and now you are only repeating it for practice.

You have a familiar already, and that is more than enough: you cannot make another.
told.copy:
Wait, I'll copy it again!

I want to be sure I have the same as you. Better to have no trouble!
